scope: Milestone 0 conservative syntax inventory, not Milestone 6 runtime enforcement or whole-program proof.

Production .go FuncDecl bodies in cmd/ and internal/, including nested function literals attributed to their enclosing declaration; _test.go and the scanner's own command are excluded. Historical migrations/*.sql are separate entries.

Session/session_threads status and enumerated owner/archive/workspace/snapshot/container gate writes; authority-table and named holder/changeset/materialization/preview/control roots; dispatch references and ordered Enqueue/EnqueueInTx/EnqueueWithTarget/EnqueueWithOpts/EnqueueInTxWithOpts receiver/tx/job/payload/dedupe argument facts. Context availability sandbox_state, bounded ListExpiredSnapshots preflight, snapshot-named Delete calls, and the exact CleanupSessionSnapshot helper's delete/clear receiver/arguments/order plus direct archive/merge callers are explicit inventory boundaries; expiry and orphan review-bundle cleanup are separate operation contracts. Exact PRService CreatePR/CreateBranch/PushChangesToPR/dispatchPostPRSnapshotUpload roots also inventory fresh-key production and pending/Save/promote/clear identity, control conditions, argument dependencies and ordered effects; otherwise generic Save methods are not globally selected.

Same-package named-function and same-receiver wrapper edges plus conservative lifecycle-named cross-package selector edges. Each entry identifies the current symbol, not a promise that it already uses the proposed canonical owner.

Hand-authored root and direct named mutation-caller contracts coexist with explicitly labelled AST syntax-only indirect wrapper rows. Current predicate/lock/stale outcome and future canonical_target/authority/fence_outcome/prerequisite_0a remain distinct. No recursive blanket authority promotion. Concrete raw/generic/named root callers cannot pass on vague future-audit notes.

source_sha256 binds normalized discovered SQL, relevant string dependencies, guard/authority expressions (including lifecycle switch tags/case lists), locks, ordered boundary/enqueue calls and conservative enqueue argument dependencies. Six exact dispatch-key helper return expressions/bindings/constants are tracked. Whole enclosing bodies and unrelated logging are not hashed. Files are parsed once for declarations and package constants; discovery never approves metadata.
limitations: No Go type checking or whole-program pointer/interface/callback/reflection analysis. Cross-package call edges are CANDIDATES, not resolved targets. Arbitrarily renamed receiver aliases, function-valued calls, helper factories and external code require manual caller review.

SQL matching is conservative lexical inspection, not a PostgreSQL parser or proof of predicate equivalence. Partial SET/dynamic target and alias-target forms are review candidates, not asserted valid statements. SQL constructed without recognizable literal/constant fragments can escape.

Package string literals/concatenations resolve across parsed files. Enqueue and exact PR-publication pipeline argument plus exact key-helper return bindings/constants are conservatively followed by identifier, without flow/scope/type analysis; renamed aliases, reassignment control flow, fmt evaluation, imports and arbitrary helper-returned payloads/SQL still need manual review. Recognizable unresolved SQL fragments remain candidates. Assignment bases recurse through identifiers/selectors/index/index-list/star/parentheses and retain index-key dependencies, but still do not resolve runtime pointer aliasing or flow.

Guard/authority/call facts use bounded vocabulary, not semantic dataflow. Switch eligibility cases and ordered enqueue argument syntax are tracked; unrelated changes containing relevant authority vocabulary may conservatively surface. Callback bodies are inspected separately with argument placeholders. Changes hidden inside arbitrary helpers remain manual-review dependencies.

Predicate and lock observations may span nested SQL/callbacks. Ordered syntax detects reordered observed locks but does not establish actual interprocedural lock order, transaction ownership, receipt authority or error propagation. Detailed M0 contracts and real PostgreSQL probes remain separate evidence.

No runtime generation/readiness enforcement, production inventory, live rollout proof, compatibility activation, or proof that an admitted dispatch consumes a particular input. Current domain fencing classifications do not mean shared admission/end epochs already exist.
Non-lifecycle candidates are exact named entries (historical SQL/integration setup/preview screenshots/lexical false positives), never broad package exemptions.

Snapshot-named Delete calls and the exact CleanupSessionSnapshot helper/direct callers are lexical candidates, not a type-resolved inventory of all object-store deletion. Reaper expiry, archive/merge cleanup and orphan review-bundle cleanup have distinct exact contracts; arbitrary blob aliases/helper effects still require manual review. Availability tombstone/notice/delete-intent fencing and fresh ordinary publication-key discipline through existing Save/Load/Delete are 0a requirements, not implemented runtime guarantees. The baseline trusts same-session workspace/native-conversation context; private bundles, isolation/export and a new immutable-storage API are optional hardening, not prerequisites. Exact PR snapshot pipeline dependencies cover local syntactic bindings/constants and helper call arguments, not arbitrary helper-return semantics or provider/storage completion proof.
